senses.def: to not have information about
a principal city of Greece
pertaining to being unable to be controlled by something or someone
senses.comment: It is also possible to translate ‘it is an evil which cannot be controlled’ as ‘it is an evil which no one can control’ or ‘no one can control this evil.’

senses.def: to pull or draw something in an upward direction
senses.comment: In a number of languages clear distinctions are made on the basis of the means by which something is pulled or drawn. For example, to pull something by means of a rope may be entirely different from a term indicating that the object itself has been seized and is being drawn or dragged.

senses.def: pertaining to not corresponding to a comparable merit or worth
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἀναξίως in 1 Corinthians 11:27, see 66.7.

senses.def: pertaining to being proper in not corresponding to what should happen
senses.comment: For another interpretation of ἀναξίως in 1 Corinthians 11:27, see 65.19.

senses.def: to be fitting or right, with the implication of possible moral judgment involved
one who is opposed to Christ, in the sense of usurping the role of Christ
senses.comment: The term ἀντίχριστος appears to have become increasingly equivalent to a proper name as the personification of all that was opposed to and contrary to the role and ministry of Christ.

senses.def: to receive something in full, with the implication that all that is due has been paid
senses.comment: It may also be possible to translate the final part of Matthew 6:2 as ‘they have received all that is coming to them’ or ‘… all that they deserve.’

senses.def: to be at some distance away from
to mark the point at which the duration of a state or process is enough
senses.comment: In a number of languages the equivalent of ‘enough!’ would be ‘that is the end’ or ‘you must stop sleeping now.’

senses.def: to experience an event to the limit of what one could expect
to keep on avoiding doing something
to wash off a part of the body

senses.domain: Groups and Classes of Persons and Members of Such Groups and Classes
senses.def: a member of the council of the Areopagus
pertaining to that which cannot be moved
(a figurative extension of meaning of ἀσάλευτος[a] ‘immovable,’ 15.4) pertaining to occurring in an unchangeable state
senses.comment: In a number of languages it may be better to express the concept of ‘enduring’ as ‘not ending,’ and accordingly one might translate this phrase in Hebrews 12:28 as ‘God’s ruling over us will never end.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to not being in accordance with what is right, appropriate, or fitting
pertaining to that which is unusual, and generally with the implication of harmful or dangerous
a person in the genealogy of Jesus

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being profane in the sense of worldly or godless

senses.comment: In most languages east and west are related to the rising or setting sun, although in some languages there may be some local geographical feature which serves as a marker of direction, for example, the location of a particular mountain, the ocean, or a river. For north, some languages employ ‘to the left of the rising sun,’ that is to say, the direction is oriented in terms of the left hand of a person facing toward the rising sun. Similarly, south would be ‘to the right of the rising sun.’

senses.def: marker of relatively weak emphasis
senses.comment: This word is frequently not translated but possibly reflected in the word order.

senses.def: to remain awake because of the need to continue alert
senses.comment: In some languages γρηγορέω in Matthew 24:43 may be rendered as ‘his eyes would be open’ or ‘he would surely see what was happening.’

senses.subdomain: Be Ready To Learn, Pay Attention
senses.def: (a figurative extension of meaning of γρηγορέω[a] ‘to stay awake,’ 23.72) to be in continuous readiness and alertness to learn
(a figurative extension of meaning of γρηγορέω[a] ‘to stay awake,’ 23.72) to remain fully alive and alert
to ask for with urgency, with the implication of presumed need

senses.subdomain: To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
senses.def: (derivative of διακρίνω[a] ‘to evaluate carefully,’ 30.109) the ability to evaluate and judge
senses.comment: In rendering 1 Corinthians 12:10 it is essential to recognize that the process of judging must have both positive and negative aspects, so that πνευμάτων must imply gifts which are genuinely from the Spirit of God and those which are not.

senses.def: to dispute with someone on the basis of different judgments
(derivative of διδάσκω ‘to teach,’ 33.224) pertaining to being able to teach
a formalized rule (or set of rules) prescribing what people must do
senses.comment: The difference between ‘a law’ and ‘a command’ is that a law is enforced by sanctions from a society, while a command carries only the sanctions of the individual who commands. When, however, the people of Israel accepted the commands of God as the rules which they would follow and enforce, these became their laws.

senses.def: an official order or decree
an emphatic marker of condition, with the implication of reduced probability

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being sincere in the sense of having pure motivation
to cause something to be excluded or not allowed
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand ἐκκλείω in Romans 3:27 as meaning that there is no basis for boasting; in other words, there is nothing that one can boast about.

senses.subdomain: Belong To, Be Included in the Membership of, Be Excluded From
senses.def: to exclude or remove someone from an association
senses.comment: It may also be possible to translate this expression in Galatians 4:17 as ‘they want you to no longer belong (to me)’ or ‘they want you to exclude (me) from your company.’

senses.def: (alternative form of Ἐλυμαῖος, derivative of Ἐλυμαίς ‘Elumais’ or ‘Elam,’ not occurring in the NT) a person who is a native of Elam
(derivative of ἐμπαίζω[a] ‘to mock,’ 33.406) one who makes fun of by mocking

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: the period of a complete year (similar in meaning to ἔτος ‘year,’ 67.167, but with the focus upon duration)

senses.subdomain: Indefinite Units of Time: Age, Lifetime, Interval, Period
senses.def: a unit of time of indefinite length, possibly somewhat shorter than αἰών[a] ‘age’ (67.143) but of a relatively uncertain reference
to exert considerable effort and care in learning something
to cause to begin and to intensify an activity
pertaining to the part of a whole which remains or continues, and thus constitutes the rest of the whole
to cause light to shine upon some object, in the sense of illuminating it
senses.comment: Expressions involving the causing of light to shine upon an object often involve explicit causative elements, for example, ‘to cause light to shine upon’ or ‘to cause to shine’ or ‘to cause to be bright’ or ‘to cause to be in the light.’

senses.def: (derivative of ἑτοιμασία ‘readiness,’ 77.1) to cause to be ready
to express in attitude and ritual one’s allegiance to and regard for deity
senses.comment: In a number of languages worship is expressed in an idiomatic manner, for example, ‘to bow down before,’ ‘to lower one’s head before,’ ‘to raise one’s arms to,’ ‘to sing to,’ ‘to honor.’ It is important in selecting an expression for worship to employ a term or phrase which will include various aspects of worship.

senses.def: to fulfill one’s socio-religious obligations
a particularly undesirable weed resembling wheat and possessing a seed which is poisonous
senses.comment: In this one passage in which ζιζάνιον occurs in the NT, it is possible to use an expression such as ‘poisonous weed’ or ‘bad weed.’

senses.def: (derivative of θάνατος[a] ‘death,’ 23.99) that which causes or produces death
to cause people to riot against
to be emotionally upset by a concern or anxiety
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret θορυβέομαι in Acts 20:10 as referring to the evident commotion caused by the fall of Eutychus from a window. Accordingly, one may translate as ‘stop this commotion; he is still alive.’

senses.def: to take by force or stealth objects from a temple
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret ἱεροσυλέω in Romans 2:22 as meaning ‘to commit sacrilege,’ in the sense of doing harm or damage to sacred objects in temples (see 53.104).

senses.def: to commit sacrilege by doing harm or damage to sacred objects in temples
senses.comment: In biblical times the damaging of valuable objects in a temple was more than simply a criminal act, since it involved a serious breach of respect for supernatural beings. Accordingly, doing harm to sacred objects in a temple would be regarded as a particularly godless deed. For another interpretation of ἱεροσυλέω in Romans 2:22, see 57.241.

senses.def: (derivative of Ἰτυραία ‘Ituraea,’ not occurring in the NT) pertaining to Ituraea
Caesarea on the coast of Palestine, south of Mount Carmel
Caesarea Philippi at the foot of Mount Hermon; see also 93.605
to announce, with focus upon the extent to which the announcement or proclamation extends
to fall from one level to another
to fall from a standing or upright position down to the ground or surface
(derivative of κατοικέω ‘to dwell,’ 85.69) a place of dwelling, whether an object or area
a province in the southeast corner of Asia Minor
to begin an association with someone, whether temporary or permanent
senses.comment: Though the Greek text of Acts 8:29 says literally ‘join this carriage,’ in reality, of course, the association is not directly with the carriage, but with the man riding in the carriage. It is therefore necessary in a number of languages to translate κολλήθητι τῷ ἅρματι τούτῳ as ‘join the man riding in this carriage.’

senses.def: to stick or cling to something
(an idiom, literally: to cling to heaven) to increase enormously the number of something, with the implication of reaching the attention of God
to decide a question of legal right or wrong, and thus determine the innocence or guilt of the accused and assign appropriate punishment or retribution
glosses: to try a case (in the passive to stand trial)
senses.comment: The process of legal judging is often expressed idiomatically. In Africa, one of the standard phrases for judging is ‘to cut a palaver,’ but other expressions in other languages may be ‘to find guilt,’ ‘to point the finger at wrong,’ or ‘to untangle strife.’

senses.def: (derivative of κρίνω[e] ‘to judge legal cases,’ 56.20) the authority or right to judge guilt or innocence
the legal decision rendered by a judge, whether for or against the accused
to judge a person to be guilty and liable to punishment
legal action taken in a court of law against someone
senses.comment: In most languages there are technical terms for lawsuits or cases in court, but where these do not exist, one may always use a descriptive phrase, for example, ‘to accuse someone before a judge’ or ‘to argue against someone in court’ or ‘to say in court that someone has done a person harm.’

senses.subdomain: To Distinguish, To Evaluate, To Judge
senses.def: (derivative of κρίνω[c] ‘to judge,’ 30.108) the content of the process of judging
to burst open, probably from internal pressure
a relatively small area of the sea which is well protected by land but deep enough for ships to enter and moor
senses.comment: λιμήν may be rendered in some languages by a descriptive phrase, ‘a place where ships are safe from the storm’ or ‘a place where ships are never damaged’ or ‘a place where ships may stay.’ In Acts 27:12 it is difficult to know whether the reference of λιμήν is to the harbor as a convenient place for the ships to stay during the winter, or to the port (that is to say, the town at the harbor) as a convenient place for people to stay during the winter. Some languages make a clear distinction between the area where ships stay and where people may stay waiting to continue their voyage.

senses.def: (derivative of μαθητεύω[a] ‘to follow, to be a disciple of,’ 36.31) a person who is a disciple or follower of someone
senses.comment: Though in the NT μαθητής generally refers to men, it is neutral as to sex distinction, and thus in a few instances in the NT also includes women (as in Acts 6:1, πληθυνόντων τῶν μαθητῶν ‘the number of disciples kept growing’). In some languages it may be important to indicate clearly the sex distinction, and in those contexts in which the twelve disciples are being referred to, obviously the reference must be to men. However, when the wider group of disciples is referred to, then some indication should be introduced as to the fact that both men and women were involved.

senses.def: (derivative of μανθάνω[a] ‘to learn, to be instructed,’ 27.12) a person who learns from another by instruction, whether formal or informal

senses.subdomain: High Status or Rank [including persons of high status]
senses.def: a state of greatness or importance
a manifestation of great power
to receive as one’s share in or as one’s part of
senses.comment: In 1 Timothy 4:3 the reference of μετάλημψιν is to the activity of eating, and therefore one may translate as ‘which God created for people to eat,’ but one should not mistake the reference of μετάλημψιν for the meaning of the term.

senses.def: to arrange for services by an offer to pay compensation or salary
a person in the genealogy of Jesus
pertaining to someone who is born out of wedlock and is thus without legal status or rights
senses.comment: There may, however, be some serious problems involved in translating νόθοι in Hebrews 12:8, especially if νόθοι must be rendered in some languages as ‘sons whose parents are not married,’ for νόθοι occurs here in a highly figurative passage speaking of God as one’s parent. It may, therefore, be necessary to employ an expression such as ‘this means you are not his real sons’ or ‘… not sons who truly belong to him.’

senses.def: extension from a source to which the element ὁ refers
a marker of cause or reason, with focus upon the source
the state of being similar to something
(a figurative extension of meaning of ὁρμή ‘rushing motion,’ not occurring in the NT) the psychological faculty of will and impulse
senses.comment: This clause in James 3:4 may also be rendered simply as ‘wherever the pilot wants it to go.’

senses.def: (an idiom, literally: an impulse happens) to make a decision to carry out some action, but with emphasis upon the impulse involved
fish intended for food or the flesh of fish as food
senses.comment: In Greek the usual meaning of ὀψάριον is a tidbit of food eaten with bread, but it occurs in later Greek in the meaning of fish, and in the NT this meaning occurs only in the fourth Gospel (compare the usage in John 6:9 with ἰχθύς in parallel passages).|Many languages distinguish clearly between terms for fish while still living in the water and fish which have been caught and presumably are to be used for food.

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to cause someone to feel strong jealousy or resentment against someone
to cause extra difficulty and hardship by continual annoyance
the relatively deep area of the sea or ocean sufficiently far from land as to be beyond the range of any protection from the seacoast
senses.comment: In order to designate the high sea or the ocean, it may be necessary in some instances to speak of ‘the sea far from land’ or ‘the sea out of sight of land.’ People who live near the ocean and are seafaring frequently have quite distinct terms for different conditions of the sea, whether, for example, it is stormy, moderately rough, or relatively calm. Languages may also use different terms in speaking of different areas of the sea or ocean. Note, for example, in English the use of China Sea, North Sea, Bering Sea, in contrast with Indian Ocean, Pacific Ocean, Atlantic Ocean. In English this contrast is relatively fixed, but it does reflect a gradation of size, since sea is used normally in speaking of smaller areas than is the case with ocean.

senses.def: (derivative of περισσεύω[a] ‘to abound,’ 59.52) that which exists in an abundance
a degree which is considerably in excess of some point on an implied or explicit scale of extent
the measurement of width
pertaining to that which occurs in many parts
senses.comment: It is also possible to interpret πολυμερῶς in Hebrews 1:1 as referring to many different occasions, and therefore it may be translated as ‘often’ or ‘many times’ (67.11). For yet another interpretation of πολυμερῶς in Hebrews 1:1, see 89.81.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
senses.def: a number of related points of time
senses.comment: It is also possible to understand πολυμερῶς[a] (58.29). Some scholars, however, understand πολυμερῶς in the sense of ‘fragmentary’ (see 63.19). For yet another interpretation of πολυμερῶς in Hebrews 1:1, see 89.81.

senses.def: pertaining to a number of different manners in which something may be done
senses.comment: In the case of this meaning of πολυμερῶς, the terms πολυτρόπως (see 89.82) and πολυμερῶς may be regarded as mutually reinforcing, but for different interpretations of πολυμερῶς in Hebrews 1:1, see 63.19 and 67.11.

senses.def: an adult female advanced in years

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to impetuous and reckless behavior
senses.comment: In some instances it may be possible to translate προπετής in Acts 19:36 as ‘without thinking’ or ‘without counting the cost.’

senses.def: the flesh of fish as food
senses.comment: In literature outside the NT, προσφάγιον normally refers to some type of relish eaten with bread, but in John 21:5 (the only occurrence in the NT) the reference is to the flesh of fish.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
senses.def: pertaining to a number of related points of time occurring with limited intervals

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
senses.def: pertaining to a number of related points of time occurring with short intervals and probably somewhat more emphatic than πυκνός, πυκνά (67.12)
senses.comment: It is possible to understand πυκνότερον in Acts 24:26 as a comparative form of the stem πυκνο, but it is also possible that any comparative force may have been lost and thus πυκνότερον would not be significantly different in meaning from πυκνά (67.12).

senses.def: the oldest son of Jacob and ancestor of an Israelite tribe
the Hebrew measure for grain, about a peck and a half or somewhat less than one-half bushel (a bushel consists of four pecks) or approximately twelve liters in the metric system
senses.comment: In Matthew 13:33 the precise amount of flour is not important. What is important is to provide some type of measurement which will indicate a considerable quantity.

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: limb of a human or animal that supports the body and is used for movement; the two human legs extend from the top of the thigh to the foot
(a figurative extension of meaning of σπιλάς ‘a rock or reef washed by the sea,’ not occurring in the NT) an unrecognized source of danger or peril
senses.comment: σπιλάς in Jude 1:12 may also be understood as meaning ‘spot’ or ‘stain’ (see 79.57).

senses.def: that which constitutes an unwanted spot or stain upon something
senses.comment: It is also possible that in Jude 1:12 σπιλάς means an ‘unseen danger,’ in that it may refer to a rock which is mostly or completely covered by the sea (see 21.5).

senses.def: a person of ordinary rank in an army
senses.comment: In some languages the normal equivalent of στρατιώτης would be ‘one who carries a gun,’ but such an expression would be completely anachronistic. Some translators have attempted to substitute a phrase such as ‘one who carries a sword,’ but this has failed in most cases since it suggests merely individual violence instead of organized warfare. It may therefore be important to use a phrase such as ‘one who fights under command’ or ‘one who is charged by the rulers to fight.’

senses.def: to give careful consideration to various implications of an issue
to confer, implying a series of proposals
senses.comment: In some languages the equivalent of ‘to confer’ is ‘to discuss what should be done’ or ‘to talk about plans.’

senses.def: to express differences of opinion in a forceful way, involving alternative opportunities for presenting contrasting viewpoints
to meet and join up with, with either friendly or hostile intent
senses.comment: In instances in which meeting up with someone may be either friendly or hostile, it is frequently necessary to select terms which will indicate clearly the relation or intention of the participants. In most languages a purely neutral term of ‘meeting’ would be misleading.

senses.def: to assist in supplying what may be needed
to fit together in a coherent and compatible manner
a region to the north and east of Palestine and known as Aram in OT times
(compare ταπεινός[c] ‘of low status,’ 87.61) pertaining to being discouraged and lacking in hope, with the possible implication of some association with low social status

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being unpretentious in one’s behavior
senses.comment: In some languages the expression ‘humble in spirit’ or ‘humble in heart’ may be expressed as ‘speaking only soft words’ or ‘without shouting at others.’

senses.subdomain: Low Status or Rank [including persons of low status]
senses.def: pertaining to having low and humble status

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: pertaining to being meek, with the implication of low status
pertaining to a particularly clear or plain visual image
senses.comment: In Mark 8:25 both διέβλεψεν (24.35) and ἐνέβλεπεν (24.9) occur. Some scholars assume that the two expressions are essentially equivalent in meaning, but others believe that διέβλεψεν is to be understood as ‘to look intently’ or ‘to focus one’s eyes upon.’

senses.domain: Body, Body Parts, and Body Products
senses.def: (derivative of θρίξ ‘hair,’ 8.12) pertaining to or consisting of hair
to come near to and to meet, either in a friendly or hostile sense
senses.comment: In a number of languages it is necessary to specify clearly by the choice of terms whether the meeting is friendly or hostile.

senses.def: to oppose in battle
to have an opinion based on scant evidence, often with the implication of regarding a false opinion as true
to speak or talk, with apparent focus upon the content of what is said
to say something in order to explain more fully the implications or intent of what has been said
to cause to carry or bear a load
glosses: to cause to bear a load

senses.def: the land west of the Jordan river

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: an event or activity which is useful or benevolent
senses.comment: In the case of χρηστός[b] (88.9) and χρηστότης[a], an equivalent often contains an expression meaning ‘to help.’ For example, the expression ‘what is useful’ is often rendered as ‘that which helps people’ or ‘that which proves good for people.’

senses.domain: Moral and Ethical Qualities and Related Behavior
senses.def: to provide something beneficial for someone as an act of kindness

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time without Reference to Other Points of Time: Time, Occasion, Ever, Often
senses.def: points of time consisting of occasions for particular events
senses.comment: In a number of languages there is no general term for ‘time’ or ‘occasion.’ In some contexts it is simply not necessary to have such a term. For example, in rendering Matthew 13:30 one may translate ‘when the harvest comes, I will say to the reapers’ or ‘when people begin to harvest, I will say to the reapers.’ In other contexts, a term which normally refers to some unit is employed in a generic sense, as in the case of Greek ὥρα which means literally ‘hour’ but is frequently used as a generic expression for a point of time, as in Matthew 8:13. In Acts 7:17 χρόνος may often be rendered by a generic expression such as ‘day,’ for example, ‘when it was almost the day for God to keep his promise.’ In the case of Matthew 26:45, the nearness of the time may be indicated as ‘very soon the Son of Man will be handed over.’`|Though it seems quite ordinary in English for one to speak of ‘time coming’ or ‘… drawing near,’ this type of figurative usage is impossible in many languages. The equivalent may be simply ‘will soon be’ or ‘is about to happen.’ The expression οὔπω ἥκει ἡ ὥρα μου (literally ‘my time has not yet come’) in John 2:4 denotes that it is not yet the occasion for a particular event (see καιρός in John 7:8 and compare John 7:10) but that it will soon be. In these contexts the expression may be rendered as ‘there is still time’ or ‘I will soon do it.’ In John 7:30 and John 8:20 (οὔπω ἐληλύθει ἡ ὥρα αὐτοῦ ‘his time has not yet come’) the reference is to the occasion of his eventual arrest, implying that it will indeed happen.

senses.subdomain: Indefinite Units of Time: Age, Lifetime, Interval, Period
senses.def: an indefinite unit of time which is relatively short
senses.comment: For languages which have no term for an indefinite unit of time which is relatively short, it may be necessary to approximate the time span in the context, for example, ‘for several months’ or possibly ‘for a year or so.’

senses.subdomain: Definite Units of Time: Year, Month, Week, Day, Hour
senses.def: one-twelfth of a day, measured from sunrise to sunset (in any one day the hours would be of equal length, but would vary somewhat depending on the time of the year)
senses.comment: Since the hours were counted beginning at sunrise, the seventh hour would be approximately one o’clock in the afternoon. For other references to numbered hours, see 60.50, 60.56, 60.57, and 60.58.

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Units of Time: Daybreak, Midday, Midnight, Late
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: much hour) a point of time relatively late in view of the circumstances (late in the afternoon or in the evening)

senses.subdomain: A Point of Time with Reference to Other Points of Time: Before, Long Ago, Now, At the Same Time, When, About, After
senses.def: (an idiom, literally: the present hour) an emphatic reference to a point of time which is simultaneous with another point of time
